task_packet.capability_success_condition: Create one coherent Tier-1 Phase 49Q PR B that is explicitly pending operator signature until merge. Add a comprehensive operator-decision ADR and make only minimal, clearly marked current-state/supersession annotations in the three named historical or gate-registry documents; do not rewrite their historical claims. The ADR must bind the merged Phase 49P intake and exact Finn/Dixie evidence SHAs, distinguish evidence from operator acceptance, and state the decision that becomes effective only if operator:eileen merges the audited PR: (1) accept Railway PostgreSQL as the bounded, reversible MVP-2 canonical-store physical host, never the Straylight product boundary or semantic owner; (2) discharge ADR-022E gate #8 only for bounded host selection and opening the provider-neutral durable-storage implementation lane; (3) resolve D.1(ii), record full D.1 satisfied because D.1(i) was already accepted, and authorize D.2/Phase 50A to start without claiming D.2 complete; (4) authorize a provider-neutral PostgreSQL StorageAdapter, canonical migrations, local/non-production integration proof, export/restore, rollback, audit-chain continuity, idempotency/concurrency, and provider-replacement work in loa-straylight under a later exact Phase 50A packet; (5) keep gates #9 and #10 HELD at PARTIAL_RECORDED for their sibling-specific runtime/boundary responsibilities, including Finn's unresolved TIER_TRUST_MAP and CRITICAL_ACTIONS findings; (6) keep MVP-2 OPEN pending Phase 50A capability delivery and Phase 50B independent proof acceptance; and (7) preserve loa-straylight as permanent semantic owner, Dixie as the current route/admission boundary, and Finn's authorized runtime-enforcement role. Carry every ADR-049 §9.1 clause, a precise authorization matrix, rollback/reopening triggers, a provider-portability contract, an evidence appendix, a gate/dependency before-and-after matrix, and a Phase 50A handoff envelope. Treat absent provider operational facts—durability, backup/restore, failover, version pinning, isolation, tenancy—as mandatory pre-production proof obligations, not as already proven facts and not as authority for production admission.
non_goals: Do not implement the StorageAdapter, migrations, SQL, schema, tests, configuration, runtime wiring, deployment, backup job, restore job, or any Phase 50A code.

Do not provision, configure, access, or mutate Railway or any external infrastructure; do not use credentials, secrets, connection strings, endpoints, account identifiers, project identifiers, regions, ports, pricing, or topology details.
Do not authorize production admission, production estate writes, production migration execution, production rollout, cutover, living-estate admission, or a claim that Railway is production-ready.
Do not authorize or implement auth, consent, signer, controller-binding, identity-mutation, challenge, revocation, forgetting, inheritance, commitment, or permanence semantics.
Do not close gates #9 or #10, resolve Finn's two locally defined classifications, impose a new Dixie substrate contract, modify a sibling repository, or transfer any semantic authority.
Do not close MVP-2, claim D.2 complete, claim Phase 50A or Phase 50B complete, or progress beyond MVP-2.
Do not make Railway a permanent dependency, embed provider-specific concepts in the estate domain model or canonical migration semantics, or define a Railway-specific adapter contract.
Do not create a Tier-2 cross-repository contract or Tier-3 estate-semantic decision; escalate if the evidence indicates either is required.

Do not treat Claude's authorship, the lane activation, PR opening, audit acceptance, or control-plane eligibility as the operator signature; only a later operator-authorized merge makes the ADR decision effective.
Do not edit historical decision text to pretend an earlier document made the Phase 49Q decision; use explicit later-status or supersession annotations only.
required_tests: Verify current main equals exact base 77030a93ec2dddef5a96a7a7e047a009043252d5 before work and before completion.
Run npm run build before typecheck or tests, then npm run typecheck, npm run control-plane:validate, npm test, and npm run control-plane:test.
Verify the complete base-to-head diff changes only the four allowed Markdown paths and that the new ADR is the only newly created file.
Run git diff --check and verify LF-only text with no tabs, trailing whitespace, placeholders, or conflict markers.
Resolve every repository path:line citation, relative link, section reference, result token, PR number, and exact SHA against the bound commits.
Independently re-read merged Phase 49P at 77030a93ec2dddef5a96a7a7e047a009043252d5 and the exact Finn/Dixie evidence artifacts before deriving the decision.
Verify all ten ADR-049 §9.1 clauses appear as enforceable conditions and are consistent with the Phase 49P P-1 through P-14 requirements.

Verify a machine-readable or clearly tabulated before/after matrix covers gate #8, gates #9/#10, D.1(i), D.1(ii), full D.1, D.2, MVP-2, semantic owner, physical host, and authorized implementation scope.
Verify the three existing documents preserve their original historical assertions and add only unambiguous later-status/supersession annotations that point to the new ADR.
Verify the decision and every summary distinguish host acceptance, implementation authorization, production admission, and product/MVP acceptance as separate transitions.
required_negative_tests: No statement may claim provider durability, backup/restore, failover, version pinning, isolation, tenancy, availability, compliance, or production readiness is already proven.
No statement may authorize production database writes, production credentials, production migration execution, living-estate admission, production auth/consent/signer behavior, or unrelated rollout.
No statement may close gates #9/#10, resolve TIER_TRUST_MAP or CRITICAL_ACTIONS, close MVP-2, complete D.2, or claim MVP-2 product acceptance.
No statement may transfer semantic ownership from loa-straylight or let Railway, PostgreSQL, Finn, Dixie, a cloud, runtime, adapter, controller, tenant, or model provider define estate semantics.
No Railway-, deployment-, or host-specific product concept, behavior, or configuration may enter the estate domain model or canonical migration semantics.
No provider acceptance may be represented as automatic acceptance of a StorageAdapter implementation, production wiring, provider operations, or Phase 50B proof.
No operator authority may be attributed to Claude, Codex, sibling maintainers, GitHub labels, an audit verdict, or the control plane.
No historical document may be silently rewritten so its earlier held/unselected state appears never to have existed.
No path outside the four allowed Markdown files may change; no second PR may be opened.
required_no_leak_checks: Scan the complete diff for credentials, tokens, keys, connection strings, database URLs, endpoints, hostnames, ports, account/project identifiers, regions, topology details, environment-variable values, pricing, commands, deployment instructions, and secret-bearing examples.
Ensure Railway is discussed only as a bounded product/provider decision and proof target; include no live infrastructure values or operational access instructions.
Ensure sibling evidence is cited by public repository path, PR, section, and exact commit only; include no local paths, hidden files, worktree details, model memory, or private session content.
task_packet.required_completion_report: Report reconstructed lane state and accepted lease; exact base, branch, head, parent/ancestry, PR number and status; complete changed-file list and per-file purpose; a decision table for host acceptance, gate #8, D.1(ii), D.1, D.2, gates #9/#10, MVP-2, Phase 50A and Phase 50B; all ten §9.1 clause locations; authorization/non-authorization matrix; provider-proof obligations; historical-annotation proof; exact validation results; citation/no-leak/negative results; completion event ID/comment; final lane state; and explicit confirmation that Claude did not sign, audit, accept, or merge the decision.
stop_conditions: Stop without changing files if current main is not the packet base, the lane does not reduce to ready-for-claude for this packet, the packet digest or branch binding cannot be verified, or another valid Phase 49Q lane/PR exists.
Stop and post a protocol-valid implementer.blocked or implementer.escalated event if any required merged evidence, citation target, or exact sibling SHA is unavailable or contradictory.

Stop and escalate if the decision would require estate-semantic changes, a Tier-2 cross-repository contract, sibling-repository edits, external infrastructure access, secrets, or additional file paths.
Stop and escalate if D.1(i)'s accepted state or the legal relationship between gate #8, D.1(ii), full D.1, and D.2 cannot be proven from merged authority.
Stop rather than inventing provider operational facts or silently weakening any ADR-049 §9.1 or Phase 49P P-1 through P-14 obligation.
Stop if the PR head moves unexpectedly, the working tree contains unrelated changes, tests fail for a production defect, or the complete diff exceeds the authorized four-file scope.
Never merge, never self-audit, and never present the draft or PR as an effective operator decision before operator:eileen separately authorizes merge.
